title: WI08 Interactive Installer UX
rawUserRequest: Complete WI-08 Interactive Installer UX from the attached AI Cockpit next-stage directive through archive, PR, merge, closure, and branch cleanup. Make the interactive installer the human default, implement the specified ten-step flow, preserve atomic rollback, and do not commit, push, create a PR, merge, delete a successful install branch, auto-activate Strict policy, or equate installation with completed calibration.

rawRequestSource.reference: conversation and attached AI Cockpit next-stage directive: WI-08 Interactive Installer UX

declaredIntent.summary: Converge the existing safe interactive installer on the specified ten-stage operator UX without weakening its transaction, rollback, automation, or calibration boundaries.

outOfScope: Replacing the existing Installer transaction engine or duplicating its rollback authority
Adding a full-screen TUI, web UI, package-manager distribution, or uvx command
Committing, pushing, creating or merging PRs from the installer
Automatically activating a Lite, Standard, or Strict calibrated project profile
Claiming installation completes calibration or production readiness
Implementing WI06 capability-claim binding, WI09 external identity controls, or WI10 end-to-end adoption validation

sources.reason: Existing read-only-until-confirmed wizard orchestration to extend rather than replace.
Existing deterministic eight-step plan model that must converge on the required ten-step contract.
Sole installation transaction and rollback authority; intentionally read-only for this Work Item.
Current public architecture and safety boundary for the interactive installer.
Executable confirmation, dry-run, localization, and delegation evidence.

riskAssessment.reason: The change alters the public human installation flow and localized decision chrome, but delegates every write and rollback to the existing tested Installer transaction.

reasons: Interactive installer orchestration, localization, and public capability evidence require the Standard route; release publication behavior is unchanged.

executionDecision.reason: The attached directive fixes the ten steps and safety boundaries, and the user has explicitly authorized bounded implementation decisions and the full PR lifecycle.

preReviewWarnings: Confirm no target write occurs before explicit affirmative confirmation.
Confirm profile selection is plan-only and does not activate Strict or claim calibration completion.
Confirm failure continues to restore the original branch or detached HEAD and pre-install filesystem state through the existing Installer transaction.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: The interactive installer presents exactly ten ordered stages: Target Repository, Readiness, Installation Mode, Governance Profile, Planned Changes, Conflict Review, Explicit Confirmation, Installation, Verification, and Next Action.
The default human entry remains no-argument TTY or ./install.sh --interactive, while explicit legacy CLI options remain deterministic and no-argument non-TTY execution fails closed without writing.
The wizard shows repository facts, a Standard default among Lite/Standard/Strict, planned add/modify counts, source-code impact, and adoption branch before confirmation.
Dry Run, blocked readiness, unresolved conflict review, or declined confirmation invokes no write transaction.
Profile selection remains advisory installation-plan evidence: Strict is never auto-selected or activated and installation is never reported as completed calibration.

Confirmed installation delegates to the existing Installer, reports verification and next actions, and preserves its atomic rollback of Git HEAD, files, managed sections, Makefile, and agent markers on failure.
English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese wizard resources remain key-parity compatible and public documentation/capability evidence matches the executable ten-step boundary.
Focused installer tests and the Contract-selected Standard quality route pass.
guidelines: Reuse read-only detection and the existing Installer transaction; do not create a second write or rollback engine.
Keep the pre-confirmation path side-effect free and make every non-affirmative outcome fail closed.
Treat governance profile selection as a visible plan choice only; calibration and activation remain separate workflows.
Keep all human-facing decision chrome in exact-parity locale resources and preserve machine facts verbatim.
Do not add commit, push, PR, merge, successful-branch deletion, or package-manager behavior.

intent.problem: The repository already has a safe eight-step installer wizard, but it does not match the next-stage ten-step human UX contract: governance profile, planned changes, conflict review, post-install verification, and next action are not first-class stages. Prompt-oriented installation guidance must become secondary to a concrete operator flow without weakening transaction safety.
constraints: Preserve the existing Installer as the sole write and rollback authority.
Perform no target write before explicit affirmative confirmation.
Keep legacy non-interactive flags compatible and no-argument non-TTY fail closed.
Default the displayed profile to Standard, never automatically choose or activate Strict, and keep calibration separate.
Preserve exact-parity English, Japanese, and Simplified Chinese locale resources.
Avoid unrelated refactoring and package-manager or full-screen UI work.
intent.rationale: Extending the existing plan and orchestration layers provides the required human comprehension while retaining the already-tested detector, transaction, and rollback boundaries.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An operator reviews a new adoption without confirming it.
scenarioCoverage.expected: All ten stages, Standard-by-default profile, planned changes, conflict state, and automation boundary are visible while the target filesystem and Git HEAD remain unchanged.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused dry-run and declined-confirmation tests that snapshot target paths and Git HEAD.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Readiness or conflict review is blocked.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The wizard stops before Explicit Confirmation and never constructs or invokes a write Installer.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Inject blocked detection and conflict facts and assert fail-closed status with zero installer calls.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A confirmed installation succeeds or the Installer transaction fails.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Success reports Verification and Next Action without calibration overclaim; failure reports restoration and relies on the existing atomic rollback path for branch/detached HEAD and filesystem state.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Run focused wizard delegation/result tests plus existing installer rollback and adoption lifecycle tests.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: Set only when a human explicitly approves restricted governance paths.
